headline: High: Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side execution and broad egress can amplify shared-state, leakage, and compliance risks when paired with marketingskills’ shared-context file workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can ingest uploaded files and arbitrary HTTP outputs into flows, and its server-side Python component is unsandboxed by default. marketingskills builds on shared context across skills and reads/writes skill files. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path through shared content, though not a direct always-on channel.
conditions: IF Langflow flow inputs include attacker-controlled text or files that marketingskills later reuses as instructions
IF shared skill files are edited from Langflow outputs without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any shared file is reused
Prefix all imported content with non-executable delimiters
Disable automatic chaining from file content to tool instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write filesystem content, and Langflow explicitly handles uploaded files plus per-flow credentials and server-side stores. marketingskills also persists marketing context in local skill files. If they share a workspace or server-side store, sensitive flow inputs can leak into marketing artifacts or logs.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same workspace or shared server-side store
IF Langflow flows process sensitive uploads or credentials and marketingskills reads those files
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credential stores
Restrict file permissions on shared directories
Review and redact sensitive uploads before reuse
Turn off persistence for nonessential flow artifacts
requires-engineering: add data-class filtering between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and network egress; marketingskills also has filesystem write, subprocess, and allowlisted egress. With shared mutable files or a common workspace, concurrent writes and side effects can collide, and Langflow’s server-side state makes this more likely in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or shared server-side state
IF either agent writes generated artifacts while the other concurrently edits them
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs on shared artifacts
Review diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents in graph-based flows, so its outputs may be treated as upstream inputs. marketingskills is a context-building skill set that can reuse shared context. That makes error propagation plausible if Langflow-generated content is consumed without verification, though marketingskills is not shown to take autonomous external actions.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes Langflow-generated text as authoritative context
IF no verification step checks facts before reuse or publication
mitigations: Require source citations before reuse
Add a human approval gate for generated claims
Compare outputs against original inputs
Limit downstream use to drafts only
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow handles per-flow credentials and uploaded files, while marketingskills stores marketing context in skill files. The profiles do not show a specific regulated data class or residency mismatch, so only a modest compliance gap is evidenced. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of stored context and secrets.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed into Langflow flows and then copied into marketingskills files
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to those shared artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared artifacts
Set short retention for flow outputs
Document deletion procedures for skill files
Review storage locations for residency
requires-engineering: align retention policies across both systems
